title: 建築構造力学Ⅰ(再履修クラス)
subtitle: Structural Mechanics for Architecture I
keywords: Reaction force and cross-sectional force 2.Definition and methods of statically determinate structures 3.Stress and strain 4.E-Learning 5.Local colaboration
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to understand its position within the field and to acquire the ability to analyze fundamental structural models such as statically determinate beams, trusses, and frames. The learning objectives include understanding the types of forces acting on buildings, calculating reactions, analyzing internal forces, identifying and distinguishing types of statically determinate structures, determining stresses and strains in members, and drawing stress distributions within cross-sections.
advice: By understanding the following 10 topics and solving practice problems via e-learning, you will develop foundational skills in Architectural Structural Mechanics I: 1. Architectural structures and structural mechanics, notation of forces, composition and decomposition of forces, and moments of forces. 2. Modeling of structures and loads, stability and instability, and reactions. 3. Stress (internal forces) and how to draw stress diagrams. 4. Reactions and internal forces of statically determinate structures (simply supported beams). 5. Reactions and internal forces of statically determinate structures (trusses). 6. Reactions and internal forces of statically determinate structures (frames). 7. Sectional properties (e.g., first moment of area, second moment of area). 8. Mechanical properties of materials (stress-strain relationships). 9. Normal stress distribution in members under bending, section modulus, and edge stress. 10. Shear stress distribution in members under bending.
books: Textbooks: Step up structural mechanics Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: Students must understand trigonometric functions and elementary mechanics. A scientific calculator is required for testing. Basic knowledge of mathematics and physics (mechanics) learned up to high school is required. Basic knowledge of science and mathematics subjects studied in the first year of university is required.

activityGoals.body: Building structure and loads/external forces can correspond to the dynamic model.
Students can determine the reaction forces of static structures.
Students can draw diagrams of axial force, shear force, and bending moment of a statically determinate structure
Students can explain the basic cross-sectional and mechanical properties of materials.
Students can draw the stress distribution of columns and beams.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Students have acquired a basic knowledge of structural mechanics. (2) Students can describe the underlying formulas and find the exact solutions to those formulas. (3) Students can represent the resulting solutions graphically. (4) Students can show a simple structural model and can calculate stress. (5) Students can present a proposal to plan a rational building from a mechanical point of view for a simple building.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Students have acquired a basic knowledge of structural mechanics. (2) Students can write the underlying formulas and understands the procedure for finding the solution. (3) Students can represent the resulting solution graphically.

lessons.content: Building structures and structural mechanics Force notation Force composition and decomposition Moment of force
lessons.assignments: Review: What is force, Force composition and decomposition Moment of force Preparation: Read all of Chapter 2 to Section 3.1

lessons.content: Modeling structures and loads Stable and unstable Reaction force
lessons.assignments: Review: Work on textbook issues and report issues. Preparation: Read all of Sections 3.2 to 3.3

lessons.content: Resultant stress How to draw a stress diagram
lessons.assignments: Review: Work on textbook issues and report issues. Preparation: Read all of Sections 3.4 to 3.6.

lessons.content: Reaction forces and resultant stress in statically determinate beams
lessons.assignments: Review: Work on textbook issues and report issues. Preparation: Read Chapter 5 and understand the definition of statically determinate trusses and how to solve a static truss.

lessons.content: Reaction forces and resultant stress in statically determinate trusses
lessons.assignments: Review: Review the node and cutting methods. Work on textbook examples and exercises. Preparation: Check the lecture contents up to the 5th lecture. Proceed with preparations for quizzes. Address report issues.
Review: Confirm ability to perform the tasks that are assigned in the 6th lecture. Preparation: Prepare for the quiz.
Review: Recalculate the unscored part. Preparation: Read Chapter 4 and understand how to calculate the reaction force and resultant stress in statically determinate frames.

lessons.content: Reaction forces and resultant stresses in statically determinate frames
lessons.assignments: Review: Work on textbook examples and exercises. Preparation: Read all of Sections 2.1-2.2. Reconfirm the integration of elementary functions. Address report issues.
Review: Centroid, cross-sectional area, cross-section primary moment, and moment of inertia. Work on textbook examples and exercises. Preparation: Read 2.5.

Review: Stress, strain, Young's modulus, shear modulus, etc. Work on textbook examples and exercises. Preparation: Check the lecture contents up to the 10th lecture. Address report issues. Work on the work subject.

lessons.content: Normal stress of a member subjected to bending Sectional modulus and edge stress
lessons.assignments: Review: the relationship between vertical stress and section force and the relationship between edge stress and section modulus. Preparation: Read all of Section 2.4. Address report issues. Work on the work subject and submit it at the 12th lecture.

lessons.content: Shear stress of a member subjected to bending
lessons.assignments: Review: Review the concept of shear stress and review the distribution of shear stress in rectangular sections. Preparation: Work on report tasks. Rearrange the contents learned so far. In particular, understand the contents after the 8th lecture. Prepare for the exam.
Review: Confirm ability to perform the tasks. Preparation: Prepare for the examination.
